Definition: adverb of the oblique cases of G5607; really:--certainly, clean, indeed, of a truth, verily.
BiblicalUsage: This little word means really, truly, of a truth. Paul uses it when the secrets of a visitor's heart are laid bare and he falls down confessing that God is truly among you, and again when he speaks of widows indeed, those who are truly alone and desolate.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God cares about what is really true, not what only looks true, and this word presses me to be honest about what I am.
